question.problem:
| $x$ | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $13$ | $9$ | $5$ | $1$ |

Consider the data sets above. You are given that $\overset{―}{x}=6$ and $\overset{―}{y}=7.$ Find the equation of the corresponding linear regression line. Round the slope and the $y$-intercept to **one decimal place** if necessary.

$y=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The equation of the regression line is given by

$$
y=mx+b,
$$

where 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{S}_{xy}}{{S}_{xx}},\,b=\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute $m:$

- First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(3-6)(13-7)+(5-6)(9-7) \\  & +(7-6)(5-7)+(9-6)(1-7) \\  & =(-3)(6)+(-1)(2)+(1)(-2)+(3)(-6) \\  & =-18-2-2-18 \\  & =-40\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, we compute the sum in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(3-6)^{2}+(5-6)^{2}+(7-6)^{2}+(9-6)^{2} \\  & =9+1+1+9 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for $m,$ we obtain 

$$
m=\frac{-40}{20}=-2.
$$

Next, we substitute into the formula for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x} \\  & =7-(-2)\cdot 6 \\  & =7+12 \\  & =19\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the regression line is

$$
y=-2x+19.
$$
